name: SSH Access
description: Grants agents SSH capability through a per-host allowlist with command-pattern guardrails for remote execution.

allowedHosts.label: Allowed Hosts
allowedHosts.description: User-managed list of hosts agents may SSH to. Each entry is a hostname (or user@host) plus a one-line description of what the host is for. Default empty refuses every SSH invocation. Add entries per project — bastion hosts, deployment targets, dev VMs.

allowedCommandPatterns.label: Allowed Command Patterns
allowedCommandPatterns.description: Comma-separated list of command-prefix patterns agents may execute on the remote. Matched as prefix substring against the remote command. Default covers read-only inspection patterns. Add destructive patterns explicitly (e.g. systemctl restart) and only after the user reviews them.
allowedCommandPatterns.default: ls, pwd, ps, df, free, uptime, journalctl --user, systemctl --user status, docker ps, docker logs, tail -n, cat, less, head

requireKnownHosts.label: Require Known Hosts
requireKnownHosts.description: When on, SSH invocations refuse unless the target host is in the user's ~/.ssh/known_hosts (prevents man-in-the-middle on first connect). When off, accepts new host keys silently (NOT recommended outside trusted networks). On is the safer default.

onCommandRefusal.label: On Command Refusal
onCommandRefusal.description: How agents respond when a command doesn't match allowedCommandPatterns. refuse blocks the invocation and surfaces the refusal. log-only allows the invocation but emits a warning. ask prompts the user per occurrence. Default refuse is the safest.

timeoutSeconds.label: Timeout Seconds
timeoutSeconds.description: Max wall-clock time agents wait for an SSH command to return. Default 30 covers typical inspection commands. Lower for snappier failure on hung connections; raise for known long-running commands (which should arguably not be on the allowlist anyway).
